ledger.claim: The trace, not the rounded trip record, governs the measurement under POL-RD-01: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 14.4 km against the optimal_distance_km of 9.0 km recorded at booking, an excess of 5.4 km and 60.0% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass on this trip's own telemetry - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01's trace-governs sentence is satisfied because the two distance fields (gps_trace 14.4, trip_record.actual_distance_km 14.4) agree.

The excess is additionally MATERIAL on the percentage limb of POL-RD-01: 60.0% of optimal is greater than the 50% material threshold, so the absolute 8.0 km limb does not need to be reached. The derived deviation status records 'material' for this trace. Materiality is what engages the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 and the remedy uplift in POL-RD-06(b).

The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 114 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval against a 10 s expected interval, 100.0% coverage, max_gap_sec of 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires. The rider therefore needs no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The admissibility pre-pass agrees: status COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0, no issues.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. Limb (a): trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-03308 and the same pickup and start timestamps (requested 2026-08-14T09:24:17, started 2026-08-14T09:32:00), so the artifacts describe the same trip. Limb (b): the excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured from an unimpaired trace. Once that is shown the burden shifts to the driver, and a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it.

No extra corroboration is demanded of this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 proviso that bites where a rider has 4 or more claims in 60 days and 1 or fewer substantiated does not apply, and the trace alone carries the claim.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, under POL-RD-02, and the fare model is METERED so this clause governs: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 13.0 optimal min) x surge 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route - 0.00 promo = a recomputed_fare of 14.99 against a charged_total of 20.66. That is a refund of 5.67, payable as 5.70 after rounding UP to the nearest SGD 0.05. It is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90%-of-charged_total full-refund share, so it issues as a partial.

A repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-06 on the named trailing-window counter alone: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which is '3 or more' (the ratio limb is unnecessary). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on its own trace, limb (b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 20.66, in place of the POL-RD-02 partial of 5.70. Both figures are stated side by side so the size of the uplift is auditable. This fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge pass-through lines, so nothing is carved out under the limb's proviso, and limb (c) additionally refers the driver to driver-conduct review.

The driver's only explanation, 'Road works.', cannot reduce the excess by a metre. There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-03308-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - I disclose that impairment - so POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run on the record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure. Because the driver names no advisory evidence ID, the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged; the trace also being unimpaired, POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged either.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver on this record. The chat log for this trip holds 0 messages, with first_message_at and last_message_at null, so there is no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor and no chat_message.waypoint_hint to test against the 200 m corroboration rule. Where the instruction is absent and the corroboration test cannot be run the clause does not exonerate, and none of the 5.4 km excess is excluded on that basis.

Nothing re-baselines the optimal route. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to recompute POL-RD-01 against. The 9.0 km booked optimal distance stands as the baseline for the excess.

Neither alternative fare model nor the pooled baseline is in play, so neither closes the rider's route to a refund. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11's bar on distance-and-time refunds on an upfront trip does not apply. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 is not engaged and no part of the excess is co-rider collection distance.

The billing shows the rider carried the whole detour: distance_charged_km is 14.4 against an optimal of 9.0, time_charged_min 18.8 against an optimal of 13.0, total_charged 20.66, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 - the exact figures the rider's claim names. I do not ask for anything on top of that: the fare carries no ERP or toll lines (0.00), so POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule is respected and no off-route gantry or airport surcharge is added to the POL-RD-02 figure.

No impairment discount caps the rider's case under POL-GEN-02. Every artifact this claim rests on - trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and both party profiles - carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with an empty issues list, so the confidence cap set by the evidence that decides the case is 1.0 and the ruling is not dragged to the 0.70 platform floor or into a POL-RD-10(1) escalation.

The dispute is filed_by RIDER and the fare is still CHARGED with 0.00 refunded, so the present state stands against the rider and every dollar of this ruling runs the rider's way under POL-GEN-03: a PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.70 at the POL-RD-02 floor, rising to the whole contested 20.66 should the POL-RD-06(b) uplift be applied, in either case leaving the rider no longer carrying the disputed charge.

The rider asks for the whole $20.66, but POL-RD-02 makes the distance-and-time refund arithmetic, not discretionary. On the platform's own figures: charged_total $20.66; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 9.0 km optimal + 0.28 x 13.0 min optimal) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + the $0.80 platform fee = $14.99; refund $5.67, rounded up to $5.70. That is 27.4% of the amount contested, not 100% of it. The meter billed 14.4 km against a trace of 14.4 km, so the only recoverable sum is the excess over the booked optimal route, not the fare for a journey the rider would have taken in any event.

The rider's only route to the entire fare is the POL-RD-06(b) uplift, and that limb licenses an uplift to charged_total; it does not compel one. The driver_profile pattern test is met (deviation_flags_90d of 3 against completed_trips_90d of 180 in the same window), but a deterrent uplift is not a measure of loss, and the rider's loss here is the 5.4 km of excess distance that POL-RD-02 values at $5.67. A full refund would hand back the $3.80 base fare, the $0.80 platform fee and the 13.0-minute optimal time charge, none of which the rider lost on this trip, and 27.4% is far below the 90% share POL-RD-02 reserves for a full refund.

Whatever distance figure the tribunal reaches, nothing may be stacked on top of it. The fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll and no surcharge line, and the GPS trace records no gantry crossing, so POL-RD-09 has no off-route pass-through to correct and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) arises: there is no phantom line to refund separately, and the distance and time lines are already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 computation. The rider's total exposure is therefore the single POL-RD-02 figure of $5.70, which must not be re-added to anything.

The explanation on file from the driver is road works, and no advisory exists that can test it: EV-ADVIS-03308-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and its only issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact and the derived advisory_area for this corridor and window is an empty list. POL-RD-03's comparison therefore cannot be run, and an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is absent from the pool is precisely POL-RD-10(5). POL-RD-13(1) narrows that trigger only where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory; the identifier EV-ADVIS-03308-01 sits on this case's evidence list and is cited here, so the narrowing does not apply, and with the deciding question carried solely by a weight-0.0 artifact the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02(2) cannot clear the 0.70 floor. The disputed $20.66 should be held, not refunded, pending a human finding on whether the detour was forced.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. Measured on the GPS trace (EV-GPS-03308, weight 1.0), this trip ran 14.4 km against the 9.0 km optimal route recorded at booking (EV-TRIP-03308), an excess of 5.4 km — 60% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km absolute), and the excess also exceeds 50%, so the deviation is MATERIAL. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 114 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, 100% coverage, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire, no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The driver's explanation ('Road works.') cannot reduce the excess by a metre. No traffic advisory is on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-03308-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13 applies: the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this case does not escalate — the driver's contrary claim is rejected on that ground. POL-RD-04 is unavailable (the chat log EV-CHAT-03308 holds no messages and no waypoint to corroborate), POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-baseline against, and POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply (fare model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null; vehicle type RYDE_X).

The money. charged_total is $20.66 (EV-FARE-03308). Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 × 9.0 + 0.28 × 13.0) × the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = $14.99; the POL-RD-02 partial refund is therefore $5.67, payable $5.70 after rounding up, which is above the $0.50 de minimis floor. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines (0.00), so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct, no billing-integrity defect arises and nothing is stacked on top of the distance-and-time figure.

The driver's profile meets the POL-RD-06 pattern test on the field the clause names: deviation_flags_90d is 3 against completed_trips_90d of 180 (the count limb alone suffices). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on its own trace, POL-RD-06(b) replaces the POL-RD-02 partial with FULL_REFUND of charged_total. The two figures are stated side by side as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 partial $5.70; uplifted figure $20.66; the uplift is $14.96. No government-set or third-party pass-through line is carved out of that uplift. The driver's argument that the uplift is merely discretionary is rejected: POL-RD-06 provides that where a pattern is established these effects follow, and the deterrent uplift is on the remedy, not on the finding.

No artifact that decides this ruling is impaired — trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown and both profiles all carry weight 1.0 — and the only sub-1.0 artifact, the missing advisory at 0.0, carries no fact; POL-GEN-02 sets no confidence discount and confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. The rider's claim that no profile-based corroboration is demanded is accepted but immaterial to the outcome.

The $20.66 fare was charged with $0.00 refunded, so the whole contested amount is returned to the rider under POL-GEN-03. The monetary effect exceeds the $8.00 execution threshold, so the refund is issued but held for release by a human reviewer under POL-GEN-05; that is a routing matter, not an escalation, and it does not stay the outcome. The driver's conduct is additionally referred to driver-conduct review.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
